content: 1. Muchadzi et al. investigated the factors influencing access to HIV care and treatment within a prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) program in urban Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2010. 2. Updated guidelines on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation, and monitoring were made available through the World Health Organization's repository, accessed on June 1, 2021. 3. Killam et al. conducted a stepped-wedge evaluation to assess the impact of providing antiretroviral therapy during antenatal care on treatment initiation rates among HIV-infected pregnant women. This study was published in AIDS in 2010. 4. Ong’ech et al. compared maternal and child health clinic models with HIV comprehensive care clinic models for the provision of services to HIV-exposed infants. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012. 5. Turan et al. designed a cluster-randomized controlled trial to study the integration of HIV and antenatal care during pregnancy in Kenya. The baseline results and methodology were published in PLoS One in 2012. 6. Grossman et al. conducted a cluster-randomized trial to evaluate the integration of family planning services into HIV care and treatment in Kenya. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2013. 7. Vo et al. assessed patient satisfaction with integrated HIV and antenatal care services in rural Kenya. Their study was published in AIDS Care in 2012. 8. Tsague et al. compared two service delivery models for PMTCT of HIV during the transition from single-dose nevirapine to multi-drug antiretroviral regimens. This study was published in BMC Public Health in 2010. 9. Winestone et al. explored the acceptability and feasibility of integrating HIV care services into antenatal clinics in rural Kenya through qualitative provider interviews. Their findings were published in Global Public Health in 2012. 10. The World Health Organization's Global Tuberculosis Report, accessed on June 1, 2021, provides comprehensive data on tuberculosis and its intersection with HIV. 11. The integration of HIV and tuberculosis services is discussed in the Web Annex to the consolidated guidelines on antiretroviral use for HIV treatment and prevention, accessed on June 1, 2021. 12. Long et al. examined the prevalence and predictors of unmet contraceptive needs among HIV-positive female sex workers in Mombasa, Kenya. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2019. 13. Khan et al. studied the unmet need for contraception among sex workers in Madagascar, with findings published in Contraception in 2009. 14. Lim et al. investigated sexual and reproductive health knowledge, contraception uptake, and factors associated with unmet needs for modern contraception among adolescent female sex workers in China. Their study was published in PLoS One in 2015. 15. Ochako et al. conducted a qualitative study on the experiences of female sex workers using contraceptive methods in Kenya. Their findings were published in BMC Women’s Health in 2018. 16. A global consultation held in Switzerland in April 2016 reviewed lessons from sexual and reproductive health programming to enhance HIV prevention for adolescent girls and young women. 17. The consolidated guideline on sexual and reproductive health and rights of women living with HIV was accessed through the World Health Organization's repository on June 1, 2021. 18. Narasimhan et al. conducted a systematic review on the integration of HIV testing services into family planning services. Their findings were published in Reproductive Health in 2019. 19. Rohwer et al. updated a systematic review on integrated services for HIV testing and family planning, which is currently in preparation. 20. Rosenberg et al. compared youth-friendly health services to standard care through the Girl Power-Malawi initiative, with findings published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2018. 21. Haberlen et al. systematically reviewed the integration of family planning services into HIV care and treatment services. Their findings were published in Studies in Family Planning in 2017. 22. Warren et al. conducted a cross-sectional survey on family planning practices and pregnancy intentions among HIV-positive and HIV-negative postpartum women in Swaziland. Their findings were published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2013. 23. Zapata et al. presented a case study on integrating HIV and sexual and reproductive health services at the Epako Clinic in Namibia. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Integrated Care in 2017. 24. Hewett et al. evaluated the cost-effectiveness of HIV and sexual and reproductive health service referral and linkage models in Zambia. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2016. 25. Siapka et al. analyzed the impact of integrating sexual and reproductive health services on consultation duration times, with results published in Health Policy and Planning in 2017. 26. Birdthistle et al. analyzed client flow data over time to assess the integration of HIV and maternal healthcare in Swaziland. Their findings were published in BMJ Open in 2014. 27. Obure et al. evaluated the technical efficiency of integrating HIV and sexual and reproductive health services in Kenya and Swaziland. Their findings were published in Social Science & Medicine in 2016. 28. Siapka et al. systematically reviewed evidence from lowand middle-income countries to assess cost savings and efficiency gains in HIV services. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2014. 29. Obure et al. conducted a cost function analysis to determine whether integrating HIV and sexual and reproductive health services achieves economies of scale and scope. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2016. 30. Ayon et al. developed integrated community-based HIV prevention, harm reduction, and sexual and reproductive health services for women who inject drugs. Their findings were published in Reproductive Health in 2019. 31. Dulli et al. conducted a non-randomized trial to address the reproductive health needs of female sex workers through integrated family planning and HIV prevention services in Kenya. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2019. 32. Milford et al. explored provider attitudes and understanding of implementing an HIV and sexual and reproductive health service integration model in South Africa. Their findings were published in the African Journal of AIDS Research in 2018. 33. Narasimhan et al. emphasized the importance of investing in sexual and reproductive health and rights to achieve HIV and universal health coverage goals. Their findings were published in The Lancet Global Health in 2018. 34. A call to action was issued to achieve universal health coverage through linked sexual and reproductive health and rights and HIV interventions, accessed on June 1, 2021. 35. Sarki et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence of hypertension in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in Medicine in 2015. 36. A scoping consultation on noncommunicable diseases and mental health conditions in people living with HIV was held in Geneva, Switzerland, in April 2019. 37. Ameh et al. evaluated the effectiveness of an integrated approach to HIV and hypertension care in rural South Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2017. 38. Rawat et al. analyzed the influence of integrating HIV care into primary health care clinics on diabetes and hypertension care in South Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2018. 39. Fairall et al. conducted a pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial on nurse-led chronic disease management in primary care in South Africa. Their findings were published in PLoS Medicine in 2016. 40. Prabhakaran et al. evaluated the effectiveness of an mHealth-based electronic decision support system for managing chronic conditions in primary care. Their findings were published in Circulation in 2019. 41. Havlir et al. assessed the use of a community health approach for HIV testing and treatment in rural Africa. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2019. 42. Rohwer et al. systematically reviewed the effects of integrated care models for diabetes and hypertension in lowand middle-income countries, with findings currently in preparation. 43. Kemp et al. reviewed implementation science for integrating HIV and non-communicable disease services in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2018. 44. Rabkin et al. emphasized strengthening the health workforce to support the integration of HIV and non-communicable disease services in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2018. 45. Chang et al. evaluated the cost and efficiency of a hybrid mobile multi-disease testing approach with high HIV testing coverage in East Africa. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2016. 46. Venables et al. assessed the acceptability of integrated medication adherence clubs for HIV and non-communicable disease patients in Kibera, Kenya. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2016. 47. Guidelines for psychosocially assisted pharmacological treatment of opioid dependence were accessed through the World Health Organization's repository on June 1, 2021. 48. Achmad et al. conducted a cohort study on integrating methadone maintenance treatment and HIV care for injecting drug users in Bandung, Indonesia. Their findings were published in Acta Medica Indonesiana in 2009. 49. Lucas et al. compared clinic-based treatment of opioid-dependent HIV-infected patients with referral to an opioid treatment program. Their findings were published in Annals of Internal Medicine in 2010. 50. Zaller et al. proposed a model of integrated primary care for HIV-positive patients with underlying substance use and mental illness. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2007. 51. Low et al. conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of opioid substitution therapy on antiretroviral therapy outcomes. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2016. 52. Guise et al. systematically reviewed and synthesized client and provider experiences with integrated opioid substitution therapy and HIV care. Their findings were published in AIDS Care in 2017. 53. Considerations for adopting and using multi-disease testing devices in integrated laboratory networks were accessed on June 1, 2021. 54. A global meeting report on molecular diagnostics integration was accessed on June 1, 2021. 55. The multi-disease diagnostic landscape for integrated management of HIV, HCV, TB, and other coinfections was accessed on June 1, 2021. 56. Obure et al. conducted a comparative analysis of the costs of single and dual rapid HIV and syphilis diagnostics in Colombia. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2017. 57. Khan and Vojnov are preparing a study on the patient impact and programmatic advantages of integrated testing. 58. Ndlovu et al. conducted a feasibility study on multi-disease testing for HIV and TB using the GeneXpert platform in rural Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in PLoS One in 2018. 59. The patient impact, programmatic advantages, and cost savings of integrated testing were analyzed by the Clinton Health Access Initiative, with findings currently in preparation. 60. Fox and Rosen systematically reviewed the retention of pediatric patients on HIV treatment in lowand middle-income countries between 2008 and 2013. 61. Mutambo and Hlongwana explored healthcare workers’ perspectives on barriers to providing HIV services to children in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in AIDS Research and Treatment in 2019. 62. Birx et al. discussed laboratory challenges in scaling up HIV, TB, and malaria programs, emphasizing the interaction of health and laboratory systems. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Pathology in 2009. 63. Nyandiko et al. evaluated the outcomes of HIV-infected orphaned and non-orphaned children on antiretroviral therapy in western Kenya. Their findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2006. 64. Kiboneka et al. analyzed clinical and immunological outcomes of a national pediatric cohort receiving combination antiretroviral therapy in Uganda. Their findings were published in AIDS in 2008. 65. Tuller et al. conducted a qualitative study on how transportation costs impede sustained adherence and access to HAART in southwestern Uganda. Their findings were published in AIDS Behavior in 2010. 66. Posse et al. analyzed barriers to accessing HIV care in low-resource settings, focusing on financial and logistical challenges.
